title: What happened in AI — Nov 23, 2026
intro: Today's builders stopped trusting a coding agent's "done" and started demanding evidence: pinned tool hashes, signed file digests, and checks written by a second model.
Measurement got harder at both ends. METR and the new HLS benchmark say frontier capability is outrunning the yardsticks, while vLLM showed agentic serving now lives or dies on KV-cache hits.
highlights: Verfy, Slipmark and Apex verify gate coding-agent output on hashes and independent checks, not on green tests.
vLLM moves the agentic KV cache to NVMe: each extra 1% cache hit was worth about 10% throughput on Kimi-K3.
HLS gives coding agents 8xH200s and 36 hours to build an inference system, graded token by token.
ScrapeBench: agents break website scraping policies about 97% of the time, even when given the policy.
ARTEX, an open-source framework for AI-agent intrusion, is spreading fast enough to draw an FBI warning.
Zhipu's GLM-5.4 is live on the Z.ai Coding Plan with vision and a 50% higher quota, but no benchmarks yet.

categories.name: Coding agents: proving what the agent actually checked
categories.summary: Four new open-source tools gate agent output on evidence: pinned tool hashes, signed file digests, independently written checks, and specs tied to behaviour.

articles.title: Show HN: Verfy – checks an AI coding agent's tool calls before they run
articles.summary: Pins MCP tool definitions by SHA-256 and blocks a tool whose description changes after approval; it also reads scripts before Claude Code runs them.

articles.title: Show HN: Slipmark – make AI agents prove what they checked
articles.summary: Binds each agent sign-off to a SHA-256 of the files it read and fails CI when any of them change afterwards; no model calls.

articles.title: Show HN: Apex verify – an independent model writes the checks your AI skipped
articles.summary: A different model writes the checks the coding agent skipped, proves they can fail, and returns ready or not ready with evidence.

articles.title: Agent_primitives – tie each app behaviour to the specs that prove it
articles.summary: Keeps each required behaviour linked to the spec that proves it, so a new agent session can't quietly weaken a spec and stay green.

articles.title: KRYN: A local coding agent and the benchmark that grades it
articles.summary: A preregistered benchmark of a 9B local coding agent found no uplift over OpenCode, and a 60% token cut made it worse; it also kept editing its own tests.

categories.name: Agent telemetry: idle time, loops, and the clock
categories.summary: Builders instrumented what their agents do between useful steps: waiting, repeating the same tool call, and losing track of elapsed time.

articles.title: My AI coding agents spend most of their time waiting
articles.summary: A timed overnight run of 11 Claude Code feature agents, Opus reviews and Codex logs found most of the wall-clock went to waiting, not coding.

articles.title: Show HN: An in-browser checker for AI agent transcripts (nothing is uploaded)
articles.summary: Drop a Langfuse, LangSmith or OTLP GenAI trace export and see where the agent went silent, looped, or kept hitting a failing tool; runs locally.

articles.title: Detecting AI agent loops without sending raw payloads
articles.summary: A runnable Python pattern that hashes tool-call payloads locally to reject repeated identical calls, with the limits of hash-only detection stated.

articles.title: Show HN: I built an MCP server that gives AI agents a reliable clock
articles.summary: AgentClock is a public MCP server that tells an agent elapsed time and deadlines, citing AgentTime research that time-estimation error collapses with such a tool.

categories.name: Agent isolation: sandboxes, clusters, and offensive agents
categories.summary: Where coding agents run became a security decision today, from sandbox choice to cluster placement, while agent-driven attack tooling spread.

articles.title: Sandboxing AI Coding Agents: Nono vs. Docker Sbx vs. Microsandbox vs. OpenShell
articles.summary: Kudelski Security compares nono, Docker Sandboxes, Microsandbox and OpenShell hands-on, with criteria and a decision table.

articles.title: How to Run AI Coding Agents on Kubernetes: Sandbox vs. Environment
articles.summary: Okteto separates the agent's sandbox from the environment it deploys into, so an agent on Kubernetes can test the app it changes.

articles.title: 'The Code Is Copied Everywhere': The AI Hacking Tool Causing Havoc
articles.summary: ARTEX, an open-source framework for AI-agent intrusion, is in use by espionage and financial attackers; the FBI has warned targets.

articles.title: AI agents violate website scraping policies ~97% of the time (NeurIPS2026)
articles.summary: ScrapeBench (NeurIPS 2026) finds agents ignore website terms-of-service scraping limits about 97% of the time, even when told the policy.

articles.title: HAproxy lead: On the use of AI-based tools to find bugs in open source software
articles.summary: HAProxy's lead developer, also on the Linux kernel security team, describes receiving hundreds of AI-assisted security reports in recent months.

categories.name: Evals: frontier capability is outrunning the yardsticks
categories.summary: Several groups argued that current benchmarks under- or over-state what models can do, and proposed harder, longer-horizon or behavioural measures.

articles.title: Humanity's Last System: Coding agents building inference systems from scratch
articles.summary: HLS gives coding agents up to 8xH200s and 36 hours to build a model-specific inference system, graded by a token-level verifier against a reference.

articles.title: AI model capabilities are improving rapidly and getting harder to measure
articles.summary: METR's Q4 update covers models up to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra and says public evidence can't yet settle how fast R&D-relevant capability is rising.

articles.title: The Most Important Charts in AI Are Wrong
articles.summary: Argues real-world deployment data falls well short of METR-style task-horizon forecasts that point to near-term superintelligence.

articles.title: Newer AI models are swearing more, and it usually means they're failing
articles.summary: Vals reports models trained after July 2026 swear more in chain of thought, and those runs usually fail, which makes it a cheap failure signal.

articles.title: How do you shortlist an agent memory system?
articles.summary: Agent Memory Leaderboard benchmarks text, coding and multimodal memory systems through participant-hosted Add/Search APIs under a fixed protocol.

categories.name: Inference economics: cache hits, long RL runs, and capex
categories.summary: The cost story today was about reuse and scale: agentic prefixes dominate serving, RL runs stretch to months, and token volume outgrows price cuts.

articles.title: Skip the DRAM Tier: MoRI UMBP Runs the Agentic KV Cache on NVMe
articles.summary: vLLM moves the agentic KV cache to NVMe; on Kimi-K3, each extra 1% of prompt tokens hitting cache was worth about 10% more throughput.

articles.title: RL Infrastructure at Microsoft AI
articles.summary: Microsoft AI describes RL runs of thousands of steps over weeks to months on thousands of GPUs, where numerical stability becomes the bottleneck.

articles.title: Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex
articles.summary: Google's token volume grew 330x from May 2024 to May 2026, yet five hyperscalers spent $230B on Q3 capex that cheaper tokens may not repay.

articles.title: How much should you spend on AI per engineer?
articles.summary: Per-engineer AI coding spend ranges from about $100 to $10,000+ a month at companies that all call themselves AI-native.

categories.name: Models and local execution: GLM-5.4 and on-prem inference
categories.summary: Zhipu shipped GLM-5.4 to its coding plan, and several teams showed models running beside private data instead of in a cloud API.

articles.title: Zhipu's GLM-5.4 Launches on Coding Plan, Adds Visual Understanding and Raises Weekly Quota by 50%
articles.summary: Zhipu's GLM-5.4 is live on the Z.ai Coding Plan with visual understanding and a 50% higher weekly quota; no benchmarks are published yet.

articles.title: Data + AI Anywhere: AlloyDB Omni integration with local models
articles.summary: Google's downloadable PostgreSQL-compatible AlloyDB Omni can now call local models such as Gemma 4 and Qwen3.8 from SQL, keeping data on-premises.

articles.title: Sovereign Skills: Porting an AI Code Audit to Inkling 2 Mini and Qwen3.8
articles.summary: Stream ported a cloud-model code-audit agent skill to run on a laptop with Inkling 2 Mini and Qwen3.8 for private code.

articles.title: Six Spare MacBook Airs Ran a Private LLM Before Lunch
articles.summary: Quickchat ran a private LLM across six retired M2 MacBook Airs with 16 GB each, freed when its dev environments moved off them.

articles.title: Sarvam Dictate: fast, accurate dictation – Sarvam AI
articles.summary: Sarvam's dictation API turns disfluent speech into intended text in English and 22 Indian languages, claimed more accurate than Gemini 3.5 Transcribe.
